structuralDecisions.decision: Skip deep architectural redesign: GET /api/reagent-sites follows the exact existing pattern already used by GET /api/items — a readJSON-backed helper, an unauthenticated app.get handler, a static data file under apps/mock-api/data/, listed in the startup console.log block.
structuralDecisions.rationale: Verified apps/mock-api/server.js directly: readItems()/ITEMS_PATH and the GET /api/items handler are structurally identical to what analysis.md proposes for readReagentSites()/REAGENT_SITES_PATH. No new base class, interface, layer, or cross-cutting concern is introduced. This meets CLAUDE.md's architect-skip criteria ('purely additive within an established pattern') exactly, so no RFC and no new component-placement decisions beyond confirming the existing shape.
tradeOffs: None beyond those already inherent in the existing items.json/readItems() pattern (unbounded in-memory JSON reload per request, acceptable at this app's scale).

structuralDecisions.decision: server.js must export the Express app (module.exports = app) and guard app.listen(...) behind if (require.main === module) so node:test can require() the app without binding a port.
structuralDecisions.rationale: server.js currently calls app.listen() unconditionally at module load with no module boundary for testability. This is the one structural gap that blocks every acceptance criterion requiring node:test coverage (AC2: unauthenticated-vs-session parity; AC4: complexity/coverage). The change is additive and backward compatible: `npm start` still runs `node server.js`, which still satisfies require.main === module and listens exactly as before.
tradeOffs: None — this is the standard Express testability pattern (export app, guard listen); it changes no runtime behavior for the existing start script.

fitness.property: apps/mock-api/server.js can be required by a test file without binding PORT, and still binds PORT when run directly via `node server.js` / `npm start`.
fitness.verification: node --test apps/mock-api — the new server.test.js imports server.js via require() and makes requests against the in-memory app (e.g. via supertest-free direct invocation or an ephemeral listen() in the test itself); a passing run with no EADDRINUSE and no port conflict confirms the guard works.

structuralDecisions.decision: New reagent-sites data and handler stay inside apps/mock-api — no new package, no shared library extraction — because this is the first of six slices splitting reagent-map-spec's D1 work, and the other five slices (reagent-map-globe, reagent-map-save, etc.) are separate, not-yet-started orders that may change the final shape of the Reagent Site domain.
structuralDecisions.rationale: Extracting a ReagentSite abstraction, a repository interface, or a shared types package now would be premature generalization (design-principles.md #7) against work that doesn't exist yet. apps/mock-api has no Clean Architecture layering today (flat server.js) — introducing one for a single read-only endpoint would be inconsistent with every other endpoint in the file and outside this order's scope.paths.
tradeOffs: If a later slice needs a richer ReagentSite domain model (e.g. expeditions referencing sites), that slice's analyst/architect will need to revisit server.js's flat structure — deferred cost, not eliminated cost.

layerBoundaryChecks.rule: No existing Clean Architecture layer boundaries apply — apps/mock-api/server.js is a flat, single-file Express app with no domain/application/adapter separation today.
layerBoundaryChecks.notes: Confirmed by reading server.js directly (loom MCP graph tools were not used — not needed for a single-file app with no directory structure to query). No dependency-direction violation is possible to introduce here because there is no inner/outer layer split to violate.

antiPatternChecks.notes: Considered and rejected extracting a ReagentSite domain abstraction now; deferred until a slice actually needs it (see structuralDecisions #3).

server.js is already a single large file housing all mock-api endpoints; adding one more unauthenticated GET in the established style does not materially worsen this. Not in scope to refactor here — scope.paths restricts this order to additive changes.
